literal: Posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yongzhou; further added Palace Attendant and Duke of Works.
idiomatic: They posthumously made him general of chariots and cavalry and inspector of Yongzhou, then added palace attendant and duke of works.

literal: Qingbin's son Bao, from youth entered service as Gentleman of the Suite.
idiomatic: Qingbin's son Bao began his career as gentleman of the suite.

literal: In Emperor Ming's time he acted for Ying Province and died in battle with Liang general Pei Zhili.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he acted for Ying Province and fell fighting Liang general Pei Zhili.

literal: Bao's younger brother Jin, in the Wuding era, was Administrator of Dongping.
idiomatic: Bao's brother Jin was administrator of Dongping in the Wuding era.

literal: His son Changshou, while still young was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, transferred to Director of the Right Bureau in the Palace Secretariat, and again added Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
idiomatic: His son Changshou, still a boy, was made regular attendant of scattered cavalry, then director of the right bureau in the palace secretariat, and again regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

literal: He followed the campaign against Liu Yilong, reaching the Yangtze.
idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Liu Yilong as far as the Yangtze.

literal: He was granted the title Duke of Kuaiji and added General Who Champions the State.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed duke of Kuaiji and made general who champions the state.

literal: In Emperor Gaozong's time he was made Inspector of Jing Province.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he was made inspector of Jing Province.

literal: In the fifth year of Heping he died.
idiomatic: He died in Heping year 5.

literal: His son Mizhen inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Mizhen succeeded him the title.

literal: Mizhen died without sons.
idiomatic: Mizhen died childless.

literal: His younger brother Zhuangde inherited the title.
idiomatic: His younger brother Zhuangde inherited the title, the record states.

literal: Diggan's younger brother Hou Tou inherited Diggan's post and was Minister of the Storehouse.
idiomatic: Diggan's brother Hou Tou succeeded to Diggan's office and became minister of the storehouse.

literal: Hou Tou's younger brother Lijin was also known for loyalty and prudence.
idiomatic: Hou Tou's brother Lijin was likewise famed for loyal care.

literal: He held the posts of Censor-in-Chief and Inspector of Bing Province and had administrative achievements.
idiomatic: He served as censor-in-chief and inspector of Bing Province with a record of good government.

literal: He was added General Who Champions the State and granted the title Marquis of Jinyang.
idiomatic: He was made general who champions the state and enfeoffed as marquis of Jinyang.

literal: On his death he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously named general who pacifies the south.

literal: Lijin's younger brother Yanchen was Minister of Writing and Marquis of Anle.
idiomatic: Lijin's brother Yanchen was minister of writing and marquis of Anle.

literal: Guzhen's collateral descendant by the sixth generation, Yu, style name Chenxing, was upright by nature.
idiomatic: Guzhen's sixth-generation collateral descendant Yu, styled Chenxing, was stiffly upright.

literal: In Emperor Ming's time he was General of the Martial Guard.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was general of the martial guard.

literal: At that time the army commander Yuan Cha held power; the hundred officials all paid respect, yet Yu alone made a long bow without kneeling.
idiomatic: Army commander Yuan Cha held the reins; every official bowed low, yet Yu alone gave a long bow and refused to kneel.

literal: Soon he went out as Pacification-West General and Inspector of Eastern Liangzhou.
idiomatic: He was soon sent out as pacification-west general and inspector of Eastern Liangzhou.

literal: [5] Liangzhou's scarlet dye was the finest under Heaven; Cha sent two thousand bolts of white silk and ordered Yu to dye them, but he refused and would not allow it.
idiomatic: [5] Liangzhou produced the finest scarlet in the realm; Cha sent two thousand bolts of white silk to be dyed, and Yu refused.

literal: Cha prompted the censor to impeach him; by post he was summoned to the capital.
idiomatic: Cha had the censors impeach him and summoned him to the capital by courier.

literal: On reexamination the charge did not stand, and he returned to his post.
idiomatic: A fresh inquiry found no case, and he resumed his post.

literal: Soon he died in the province, aged fifty.
idiomatic: He soon died in office, aged fifty.

literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Shuozhou.
idiomatic: He was posthumously named general who pacifies the north and inspector of Shuozhou.

literal: His son Jian.
idiomatic: His son was Jian.

literal: In the Wuding era he was Opening Office Libationer.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was opening-office libationer.

literal: The historiographer says: Zhang Sunfei, with hair tied up, served within the palace; fierce and renowned, wherever the army's edge pointed none failed to scatter and flee — foes of Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, a match for ten thousand men, would not be too much to praise.
idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Zhang Sunfei entered palace service still wearing bound hair; his martial fame blazed abroad, and wherever his armies turned enemies broke and ran — even rivals of Guan Yu and Zhang Fei would scarcely outshine him.

literal: Han had his father's bearing, did not let the ancestral structure fall, and at a parent's funeral added ceremony — there was reason for it indeed!
idiomatic: Han bore his father's spirit and did not let the family name decline; the extra rites he observed at mourning had their ground.

literal: The Wei Guzhen brothers, loyal and brave, stirred themselves to zeal and, for righteousness, forgot life.
idiomatic: The Wei brothers were loyal and fierce, roused to the utmost pitch, and for duty's sake forgot their lives.

literal: Juan's martial prestige stood out in his age, augmenting and elevating the clan enterprise — rank robes and command banners were also what was fitting!
idiomatic: Juan's renown in arms shone in his day and raised the house higher still — purple rank and commanders' pennons suited such a man.

literal: Collation notes
idiomatic: Textual notes

literal: Pursued and beheaded reaching below the Great Wall. Cefu juan 381
idiomatic: "Pursued and beheaded to below the Great Wall": Cefu, juan 381

literal: 〈page 4528〉
idiomatic: folio 4528

literal: "Great Wall" is written as "their city."
idiomatic: "Great Wall" appears as "their city."

literal: Commentary: On examination Helong is very far from the ancient Great Wall; suspecting "their" is correct.
idiomatic: Note: Helong lies far from the old Great Wall; "their [city]" is likely right.

literal: Yuele tribe. Commentary: "le" should be the error for "qin"; see the collation entry on the Yuele clan in juan 113.
idiomatic: Yuele tribe: "le" is likely a corruption of "qin"; see the Yuele clan note in juan 113.

literal: The same below; not listed again.
idiomatic: The same below; not listed again, the record states.

literal: The eighth son Guan. Northern History juan 20, Wei Guzhen biography, reads "Guan" as "Huan."
idiomatic: "The eighth son Guan": Northern History juan 20, Wei Guzhen's life, has "Guan" as "Huan."

literal: Wei shu must have changed it to avoid the taboo on Gao Huan.
idiomatic: Wei shu likely altered the name to avoid the taboo on Gao Huan.

literal: Advanced to Duke of Yuyang. In various editions "yu" (fish) is written as "yuan" (source).
idiomatic: "Advanced to duke of Yuyang": editions read yu (fish) as yuan (source).

literal: Northern History juan 20 reads "Prince of Yuyang" and omits the matter of advancement from duke to prince.
idiomatic: Northern History juan 20 has "prince of Yuyang" and drops the promotion from duke to prince.

literal: On examination, in juan 5 of the Annals of Emperor Gaozong, in the first month of the third year of Taian appears "Duke of Yuyang Wei Juan," and in the fifth month of the fourth year of Heping it records "Prince of Yuyang Wei Juan died."
idiomatic: Gaozong's annals, juan 5, Taian year 3, month 1, records "Duke of Yuyang Wei Juan"; Heping year 4, month 5, records "Prince of Yuyang Wei Juan died."

literal: There is no commandery named Yuanyang; now emended accordingly.
idiomatic: No commandery called Yuanyang exists; emended accordingly.

literal: Inspector of Eastern Liangzhou. Northern History juan 20 lacks the character "eastern."
idiomatic: "Inspector of Eastern Liangzhou": Northern History juan 20 omits "eastern."

literal: Commentary: "Eastern Liangzhou" is unattested; the character "eastern" must be a superfluous addition.
idiomatic: Note: "Eastern Liangzhou" is unattested; "eastern" is likely a stray character.
